Lines 342-348 show mechanism = "crates/athena-core/src/exploration.rs: a bounded Experiment ...", owner = "Dionysus", and measure = "Shown by the tests run with cargo test -p athena-core exploration; no athena status line prints it; status: not shown". criteria.criterion: crates/athena-core/src/exploration.rs exists, is declared in crates/athena-core/src/lib.rs, and defines a bounded-experiment type (hypothesis, unconventional approach, bound, outcome) with a validate function.
criteria.evidence: From reading the diff: exploration.rs adds `pub struct Experiment { hypothesis, approach, bound: u32, outcome: Outcome }`, an `Outcome` enum (Pending/Completed/Stopped), a `Refusal` enum, `pub fn validate(&Experiment) -> Result<(), Refusal>` and `pub fn conclude`. lib.rs adds `pub mod exploration;`.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core exploration`: tests show that an experiment with no bound or an empty hypothesis is refused, that a bounded one is accepted, and that an experiment which exceeds its bound is reported as stopped. Each test fails if validate is stubbed to accept everything.
criteria.evidence: I ran the command: 5 passed, 0 failed (exploration_refuses_unbounded, _refuses_empty_hypothesis, _refuses_empty_approach, _accepts_bounded, _reports_exceeded_bound_as_stopped). I did not edit the code, so the stub check below comes from reading the tests. If validate always returned Ok(()), the three refuses_* tests would fail because they assert Err. The stopped test would fail on its second assert, which expects Err(Unbounded) from conclude with bound 0. exploration_accepts_bounded would still pass. No acceptance test can fail when validate accepts everything, so that part of the criterion is met for every test that could be affected.

findings.summary: Nothing calls the mechanism: no Dionysus role, pipeline step or command uses exploration.rs
findings.evidence: Grepping crates/ for 'Dionysus' or 'exploration::' finds only exploration.rs itself. The user accepted a pure-code module, so this is within the reading. Still, the requirement is met only by a model type, not by anything Dionysus actually runs. Wiring it into a proposal flow is a natural follow-up.

findings.summary: Unbounded is encoded as a zero sentinel, and the `outcome` field is never set or read
findings.evidence: `bound: u32` with "Zero means no bound". Option<NonZeroU32>, or NonZeroU32 alone, would make an unbounded experiment impossible to construct instead of checking for it at run time. `conclude` returns an Outcome but never writes Experiment.outcome, so that field is dead weight.

summary: Pass. The change gives OLY-2-15 a mechanism. A new athena-core module, exploration.rs, models a Dionysus bounded experiment: it has a hypothesis, an approach, a bound and an outcome. `validate` refuses an experiment whose hypothesis or approach is empty or that has no bound, and `conclude` reports one that runs past its bound as Stopped. docs/spec.toml now names this module as the mechanism, keeps owner Dionysus, and has a measure that ends with `status: not shown` and names the test. I ran `cargo test -p athena-core exploration` and all 5 tests passed. I checked by reading the tests, not by editing the code, that every refusal test and the stopped test would fail if validate accepted everything. The one acceptance test passes either way, which is unavoidable. fmt, clippy and the full test suite passed in Athena's recorded CI checks. The changed files match the expected deliverables. Two minor findings, neither blocking: nothing calls the module yet, so it is a model rather than something Dionysus runs (consistent with the accepted reading), and an unbounded experiment is marked by bound = 0 rather than ruled out by the type, while the `outcome` field is never used.
